title: Small LLMs can be good coldstart recommenders
authors: Eugene Noel, Erika Legaspi, Rhandley D. Cajote, John Paul B. Vergara, Paul Daniel B. Santos
tldr: Demonstrates that small LLMs (<2B parameters) fine-tuned with LoRA can outperform traditional sequential recommenders (GRU4Rec, SASRec, BERT4Rec) in coldstart settings by using novel token-level analysis of item ID sequences on MovieLens10M and Yoochoose-clicks datasets.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional sequential recommenders (GRU4Rec, SASRec, BERT4Rec) struggle in coldstart scenarios where new users and items have limited interaction history. Large LLMs (7B+) used as recommenders are computationally expensive. It is unknown whether small LLMs (<2B params) can effectively learn sequential recommendation patterns or simply memorize item ID formats.
approach: Fine-tuned two small LLMs (<2B parameters): Danube-1.8B and Gemma-2B with QLoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
Formulated sequential recommendation as language modeling: serialize user interaction sequences as text strings with item IDs and special tokens.
Token-level analysis to distinguish between semantic pattern learning vs. simple digit-level exploitation of item ID numbers.
Two training strategies: full-text sequence training and single-next-item prediction to understand different learning dynamics.
Evaluation on two benchmark datasets: MovieLens10M (large, dense) and Yoochoose-clicks (sparse, real-world e-commerce).
Metrics: HitRate@1, HitRate@5, HitRate@10, MRR, NDCG@5, NDCG@10.
Comparison against five baselines: GRU4Rec, SASRec, BERT4Rec, BERT4Rec-BERT, and BERT4Rec-CF.
findings: num: Gemma-2B achieved highest HitRate@1 on MovieLens10M (0.1019), slightly outperforming Danube-1.8B (0.0995) and all baselines.
num: On Yoochoose-clicks, Danube-1.8B achieved HitRate@1 of 0.0555, Gemma-2B 0.0540, both outperforming baselines.
num: Inference latency: Gemma 59.5ms/token, Danube 34.3ms/token, far faster than 7B+ models.
cat: Token-level analysis revealed LLMs learn semantic patterns beyond simple digit exploitation: model attention focuses on meaningful item co-occurrences.
cat: Memory footprint remains constant regardless of catalog size (unlike traditional recommenders requiring large embedding tables).
cat: Small LLMs with LoRA fine-tuning achieve comparable or better coldstart performance than dedicated sequential recommenders.
cat: Full-text sequence training produces better understanding of sequential patterns than single-next-item prediction approach.
cat: Coldstart advantage of LLMs stems from their ability to leverage pre-existing language knowledge for understanding structured sequences.

definitions.definition: The challenge of making accurate recommendations when little or no historical interaction data is available for new users or items.
A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that decomposes weight updates into low-rank matrices, reducing trainable parameters by orders of magnitude.
A methodology for examining LLM behavior at the individual token level to distinguish between pattern learning and memorization.
A recommendation paradigm that models user behavior as ordered sequences of interactions to predict the next item a user will engage with.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Establishes that small LLMs (<2B parameters) with LoRA fine-tuning are viable for coldstart recommendation, offering better performance than dedicated architectures while maintaining constant memory footprint and affordable inference cost. Provides novel token-level analysis methodology for understanding LLM recommendation behavior.
directly_justifies: Odin can use small LLMs with LoRA for coldstart recommendation tasks in financial contexts (e.g., new user onboarding, new product recommendation).
Token-level analysis is a useful methodology for evaluating whether LLMs truly learn recommendation patterns.
Memory efficiency of LLMs over traditional embedding-table recommenders for large-catalog financial product recommendation.
limits: Tested on movie and e-commerce datasets; not validated on financial recommendation tasks.
HitRate@1 remains low (<10.2% on MovieLens, <5.6% on Yoochoose) leaving room for improvement.
Only tested with items-as-tokens approach; other item representation strategies not explored.
Limited to two small LLMs (Danube-1.8B, Gemma-2B); results may not generalize to other architectures.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Algorithmic Philippine-authored paper on LLM-based recommendation systems. Covers ML development, foundation models, computational efficiency, and coldstart data scenarios.

limitations: Benchmarked only on general-domain recommendation datasets (movies, e-commerce clicks), not financial recommendation tasks.
HitRate@1 performance is modest; model is better suited for top-5/top-10 recommendation.
Only two small LLMs tested; findings may not extend to other architectures or larger small LLMs.
Item representations limited to tokenized IDs; semantic item features not incorporated.
No ablation on LoRA rank or quantization effects on recommendation quality.
remember_this: Small LLMs (<2B params) with LoRA outperform GRU4Rec, SASRec, BERT4Rec in coldstart settings.
Constant memory footprint regardless of catalog size; 34-59ms/token inference latency.
Token-level analysis proves LLMs learn sequential patterns, not just digit-level exploitation.
Full-text sequence training beats single-next-item prediction for learning recommendation behavior.
